title: What If Every Wildebeest Vanished From the Serengeti?

scenes.text: What if every wildebeest vanished? The Serengeti would likely burn more.
When the disease rinderpest was eradicated, wildebeest numbers erupted and fire across the Serengeti shrank.
Before that, with few grazers, the Serengeti was a net source of carbon, not a store of it.
The Mara River would change too. About six thousand wildebeest drown there in an average year, adding roughly eleven hundred tons.
Those carcasses feed the river for years. They made up thirty-four to fifty percent of common fish diets, and bones release phosphorus for up to seven years.
Take away one grazer and fire, carbon and a river's food web all shift. A migration is an engine.

description:
What if every wildebeest vanished from the Serengeti?
Research suggests fires would spread, the savanna would store less carbon, and the Mara River would lose thousands of tons of carcass nutrients a year.
